Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Amsterdam UMC (VUmc) | 15 Feb 2025
Clinical context: Rising PSA (8.4 ng/mL) alongside a previously positive biopsy, raising suspicion for prostate malignancy.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic parenchyma spans 78.0 mL. A distinct hypointense focus occupies the right mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring roughly 12 by 9 mm. Restricted diffusion characterizes this area on DWI, mirrored by attenuated signal on the ADC map. Early focal enhancement appears on dynamic contrast sequences compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles maintain normal morphology. No evidence of extracapsular extension or suspicious lymph nodes. Bladder and rectal walls appear intact.

IMPRESSION:
1. PI-RADS 4 lesion situated in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
2. Prostate volume 78.0 mL, yielding a PSA density of 0.1 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.44532543

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient underwent clinical review on 29 October 2024 after PSA levels increased to 6.7 ng/mL, a jump from the 4.0 ng/mL recorded in July. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was subsequently performed, returning a positive result for low-grade adenocarcinoma (Gleason 3+3).
